title: Generic functions and types, constraints and type inference

videos.script: Lesson 30 showed why Go has type parameters. This lesson writes them. {{map}} First, functions with more than one. A Map that turns a slice of one type into a slice of another. The compiler reads the types off the arguments, and you will watch where that stops working. {{constraints}} Then the part after the type parameter's name. It is an interface, and it describes a set of types. You will see why a plain list of types refuses the Celsius type of lesson 10, and the one character that fixes it. {{stack}} Then a type with a type parameter: a stack that holds strings, or ints, or anything else. Its methods, its zero value, and the one thing every method of it must accept. {{methods}} Last, a method with type parameters of its own, and why no interface can ask for one. By the end you can read any signature in the slices package, and write a container of your own.
